cat-rijkshuisstijl.reason: The core job: apply the national government house style with one choice. The first thing to demo.

cat-municipal-sets.reason: Picking your own municipality from ready-made sets is the reason the app exists; no competitor offers it.

cat-bigcity-systems.reason: The big city design systems are the showcase sets for the demo and the most visible NL Design System users.

cat-vng.reason: Municipal associations and shared services are a real customer group that needs its own set from day one.

cat-lasuite.reason: Needed for sovereign workplace bundles (MijnBureau, EDIC) that are procured as a suite, not for one Dutch organisation.

cat-searchable-picker.reason: Gap decision defer: no demand, no competitor rates yes; the current picker works for the catalogue size.

cat-swatch-preview.reason: Admins choosing from dozens of sets need to see the colours before applying; competitors only partly offer it.

cat-stock-option.reason: A demo must be able to switch the house style off again cleanly; it shows the app is safe to try.

cat-completeness-badge.reason: Useful signal for set maintainers, but no competitor offers it and no demand row asks for it.

cat-design-system-choice.reason: Organisations need to pick high contrast or a softer theme, not only a brand; part of daily configuration.

cat-design-system-docs.reason: Gap decision defer: partial, no demand, no competitor rates yes.

cat-community-sets.reason: Organisations that are not municipalities, such as agencies, need their brand set to use the app at all.

cat-starter-templates.reason: Table stakes: four of five competitors offer a starting template instead of a blank theme.

cat-marketplace.reason: Only openDesk rates yes and there is no demand row; the bundled catalogue covers the need.

cat-provincial-sets.reason: Gap decision defer: no demand row and no competitor; provinces and water boards are not yet customers.

app-one-click.reason: Rebranding the whole workspace and login in one action is the core flow to demonstrate.

app-diff-dialog.reason: Seeing exact value changes matters when admins manage many sets and overrides at scale; no competitor rates yes.

app-choose-what-changes.reason: Fine-grained admin control over which values to take over; no competitor rates yes.

app-no-reload.reason: An instant repaint is what makes the demo convincing; three competitors offer it.

app-live-preview-shell.reason: Two competitors rate yes; admins need to see the result before applying it to everyone.

app-login-preview.reason: No competitor rates yes and no demand row; the shell preview covers the daily need.

app-trial-session.reason: Trying a theme safely on a live instance matters for large organisations; two competitors only partly offer it.

app-trial-banner.reason: Belongs with the trial session, which is a production safety feature.

app-trial-publish.reason: Belongs with the trial session; two competitors rate yes but it only matters once trials are in use.

app-trial-discard.reason: Belongs with the trial session, which is a production safety feature.

app-component-playground.reason: Only openDesk rates yes and there is no demand row; the shell preview is enough for most admins.

app-primary-lock.reason: All competitors are partial; a fine-grained admin choice that matters for strict house style compliance.

app-runtime-no-deploy.reason: Changing the brand from an admin screen without a deploy is the core promise of the demo.

app-scheduled-switch.reason: No competitor rates yes and there is no demand row.

app-rollback-history.reason: Version history and rollback are audit and hardening needs for tenders; four competitors are partial.

app-reset-core.reason: Two competitors rate yes; an admin needs a way back to stock values when configuring for real.

app-simple-theme-switch.reason: A feature request and two competitors rate yes; brand switching must work for non-specialists.

aut-upload-css.reason: An organisation without a bundled set needs to bring its own house style to use the app.

aut-upload-dtcg.reason: Importing the W3C token format is a migration path; only Tokens Studio rates yes.

aut-upload-validate.reason: Uploads without validation give broken themes; needed as soon as organisations upload their own set.

aut-upload-security.reason: Refusing script in uploaded styles is a security baseline for any upload feature on a live instance.

aut-custom-list-delete.reason: Three competitors rate yes; managing your own uploaded sets is basic administration.

aut-custom-export.reason: Export for reuse elsewhere is a migration feature; three competitors rate yes but it is not daily work.

int-openproject-set-file.reason: Integration with the OpenProject plugin; matters for suite deployments, no competitor offers it.

aut-dark-colours-from-file.reason: Fine-grained control over dark mode for brands that define their own dark palette; no competitor offers it.

int-menu-colour-role.reason: Integration with the OpenProject plugin shell; matters only in suite deployments.

aut-colour-notation-kept.reason: Round-trip fidelity of colour notation is a nicety with no demand row and no competitor.

aut-convert-nlds-theme.reason: Converting existing NL Design System themes is a migration and import path for organisations moving over.

aut-token-editor.reason: Table stakes: three competitors rate yes for editing colour tokens in the browser.

aut-token-editor-tabs.reason: Two competitors rate yes; grouped tokens make the editor usable for daily changes.

aut-token-reset.reason: Two competitors rate yes; undoing one edit is basic editor hygiene.

aut-token-live.reason: Three competitors rate yes; seeing an edit take effect is table stakes for an editor.

aut-overrides-persist.reason: Every competitor rates yes; edits that do not survive a restart make the editor useless.

aut-save-as-new-theme.reason: The drawn board canon asks for it; a real organisation keeps its edits as its own named theme.

aut-overrides-import-export.reason: Three competitors rate yes; moving edits between instances is a migration and OTAP need.

aut-custom-css.reason: Only openDesk rates yes; free-form CSS is an escape hatch for demanding deployments.

aut-custom-css-sanitise.reason: Belongs with free-form CSS, which is a production feature; required hardening once it exists.

aut-component-scoped.reason: Fine-grained per component control; one competitor yes, matters for strict design systems.

aut-dark-variant-auto.reason: Dark mode is an accessibility expectation and most sets have no hand-made dark palette.

aut-semantic-aliases.reason: Gap decision defer: partial, no demand, only Tokens Studio rates yes.

aut-token-math.reason: Decided no: only Tokens Studio offers it, no demand, outside the core job.

aut-multi-brand-themes.reason: Three competitors rate yes; several brands in one source matters for multi-organisation and suite deployments.

aut-figma-sync.reason: Decided no: only Tokens Studio offers it, no demand, outside the core job.

aut-git-sync.reason: Versioning the token source in Git is a config-as-code need of large deployments; two competitors rate yes.

aut-multi-platform-export.reason: Decided no: only Tokens Studio offers it, no demand, outside the core job.

aut-colour-only-ui.reason: Two competitors rate yes; a simple brand form is how a small organisation without a token set starts.

typ-bundled-open-fonts.reason: The house style only looks right with its fonts; self-hosted open fonts are part of the core demo.

typ-air-gapped.reason: Government instances often run on-premise under a strict content security policy; fonts must still work.

typ-upload-font.reason: Many government brands use a licensed font that cannot be bundled; one competitor rates yes.

typ-font-validate.reason: Belongs with font upload; checking format and size is the security baseline for any upload.

typ-font-list-delete.reason: Belongs with font upload; managing uploaded fonts is basic administration.

typ-font-login.reason: Polishing the login page with the own font matters for strict brand compliance; no competitor rates yes.

typ-marianne-gated.reason: Only for French State deployments entitled to Marianne; no demand row and no competitor.

typ-font-tokens.reason: Two competitors rate yes; font family, size and weight are part of every house style.

typ-dyslexia-font.reason: Decided no: the per-user dyslexia font is Nextcloud server's own theme; per-user settings are a non-goal.

typ-org-font-library.reason: Gap decision defer: partial, no demand, only Microsoft 365 rates yes.

ast-logo-sync.reason: A house style without the organisation logo is not convincing; part of the one-click demo.

ast-background-sync.reason: The login background should match the house style for a real organisation going live.

ast-upload-logo.reason: Table stakes: three competitors rate yes and every organisation needs its own logo.

ast-upload-background.reason: Table stakes: two competitors rate yes and most organisations change the login background.

ast-favicon.reason: Table stakes: four competitors rate yes for setting the browser tab icon.

ast-icon-library.reason: A government icon library is useful for other apps but no competitor offers it and no demand row asks.

ast-org-logos.reason: Bundled organisation logos are convenient; no competitor offers them and no demand row asks.

ast-icon-pack.reason: Decided no: no competitor, no demand, outside the core job.

ast-icon-pack-indicator.reason: Shows a state that has no demand of its own; the icon pack itself was decided no.

ast-icon-contrast.reason: Gap decision defer: partial, no demand, only Nextcloud Theming rates yes.

ast-dark-logo.reason: Only Nextcloud Theming rates yes and there is no demand row.

ast-brand-images.reason: Decided no: only Microsoft 365 offers it, no demand, outside the core job.

sur-all-pages.reason: Styling every page, including other apps, is what separates the app from portal-only theming; core demo.

sur-conduction-apps.reason: Conduction customers expect every fleet app to follow the house style through shared tokens.

sur-login-page.reason: The login page is the first screen anyone sees; four competitors rate yes and it belongs in the demo.

sur-header-nav.reason: Header and navigation carry the brand colour; three competitors rate yes and it is the first visible change.

sur-openproject-in-app-menu.reason: Integration with the OpenProject plugin for suite deployments; no competitor offers it.

sur-shell-pixel-check.reason: Guarding the shell against platform release changes is hardening for running at scale.

sur-shell-canon-check.reason: Keeping several products on the same shell canon is a suite and hardening concern.

sur-menu-labels.reason: Only Nextcloud Theming rates yes and there is no demand row.

sur-hide-slogan.reason: A simple setting government organisations change because the Nextcloud slogan does not fit them.

sur-public-pages.reason: Table stakes: three competitors rate yes; citizens see share pages without an account.

sur-email.reason: Notification emails reach citizens and staff; they must carry the house style from day one.

sur-email-footer.reason: A compliance footer on every email is a legal and tender demand; one competitor rates yes.

sur-component-bridge.reason: Mapping Utrecht component tokens gives fidelity for strict design systems; no competitor offers it.

sur-nc-variable-mapping.reason: Without mapping every Nextcloud variable, stock colours leak through and the demo looks broken.

sur-error-contrast.reason: Readable error and status messages are a WCAG requirement for any government organisation.

sur-status-tokens.reason: Status colours are part of every house style; all competitors offer it partly.

sur-mobile-desktop-clients.reason: Decided no: the official clients read core theming; owned by Nextcloud server.

sur-office-suite.reason: Decided no: no competitor, no demand, and the office editor is out of reach.

sur-custom-domain.reason: Two competitors rate yes; an own domain is mostly hosting configuration and matters at deployment scale.

sur-footer-links.reason: Dutch government sites must link privacy and accessibility statements; two competitors rate yes.

sur-web-app-name.reason: Two competitors rate yes; an organisation renames the product to its own workspace name.

sco-per-app-exclude.reason: Fine-grained admin control for testing on large instances; no competitor rates yes.

sco-per-group.reason: Several brands on one shared instance is a multi-tenant need; only Nextcloud Theming rates yes.

sco-group-priority.reason: Belongs with per-group theming, which is a multi-tenant production feature.

sco-login-unaffected.reason: Belongs with per-group theming, which is a multi-tenant production feature.

sco-user-choice.reason: Two competitors rate yes; users with low vision need to choose dark or high contrast themselves.

sco-user-follow-os.reason: Two competitors rate yes; following the OS accessibility preference is an accessibility baseline.

sco-per-site.reason: Decided no: per-group theming spec requires anonymous pages to use the instance default.

sco-per-domain.reason: Decided no: a recorded non-goal; per-domain mapping belongs to the domain theming app.

sco-tenant-isolation.reason: Decided no: only Liferay offers it, no demand, outside the core job.

sco-app-token-catalogue.reason: An integration for other apps that build their own pickers; no competitor rates yes.

acc-contrast-on-upload.reason: Government organisations must meet WCAG; a contrast warning on upload prevents publishing an unreadable set.

acc-contrast-evaluate.reason: A contrast check for other apps is an integration; no competitor rates yes.

acc-shipped-audit.reason: Organisations rely on the bundled sets meeting WCAG; this is the accessibility baseline of the catalogue.

acc-contrast-report-doc.reason: A published report per set is audit evidence for tenders; no competitor rates yes.

acc-compliance-report.reason: An evidence report for audits is a tender and law driven need, not daily work.

acc-compliance-cli.reason: Scripted compliance reporting matters for large or automated deployments.

acc-high-contrast-set.reason: An instance-wide maximum contrast theme is an accessibility need of real organisations; Nextcloud offers it.

acc-forced-colors.reason: Gap decision defer: partial, no demand, only Microsoft 365 rates yes.

acc-dark-mode.reason: Two competitors rate yes; dark mode of the house style is an accessibility expectation.

acc-dark-generate-cli.reason: Command line regeneration of dark variants is an operations task for scripted deployments.

acc-focus-indicators.reason: Visible focus is a WCAG requirement for keyboard users in every government deployment.

acc-reduced-motion.reason: Respecting reduced motion is a WCAG expectation; two competitors rate yes.

acc-keyboard-admin.reason: The settings page itself must be keyboard operable to meet WCAG for administrators.

acc-vocabulary-audit.reason: Checking the full token vocabulary is hardening for set maintainers; no competitor rates yes.

acc-block-inaccessible.reason: Decided no: contrast failures are non-blocking warnings by recorded spec decision.

acc-contrast-in-editor.reason: Decided no: only Microsoft 365 offers it, no demand, outside the core job.

acc-accessibility-statement.reason: Decided no: the report is evidence only; the statement needs an expert WCAG-EM evaluation.

gov-admin-only.reason: Every competitor rates yes; only administrators may change the theme of a real instance.

gov-delegated-role.reason: Table stakes: four competitors rate yes; communication staff, not admins, usually own the brand.

gov-audit-log.reason: Audit of who changed what is a tender and governance demand; two competitors rate yes.

gov-audit-export.reason: Exporting the audit log for an auditor belongs with the audit log, a production feature.

gov-audit-append-only.reason: A tamper-proof audit log is hardening that tenders ask for.

gov-otap-bundle.reason: Promoting configuration through test, acceptance and production is how large organisations deploy; one competitor yes.

gov-otap-cli.reason: Scripted OTAP deployments matter at scale; openDesk rates yes.

gov-federated-share.reason: No competitor offers it and no demand row asks; still building.

gov-config-as-code.reason: Two competitors rate yes; declaring the theme in Helm values is how hosted platforms run at scale.

gov-approval-workflow.reason: Decided no: only Tokens Studio offers it, no demand, outside the core job.

gov-app-store-install.reason: Two competitors rate yes; installing and updating from the app store is how an organisation gets the app.

gov-open-source.reason: Dutch government policy requires open source by default; procurement checks this before any use.

gov-licence-clarity.reason: Stating licences of bundled assets is a tender and compliance demand; openDesk rates yes.

syn-upstream-generated.reason: Sets generated from the official NL Design System sources are what makes the catalogue trustworthy.

syn-nightly-pr.reason: Gap decision defer: partial, no demand; auto-download to the instance is a recorded non-goal.

syn-freshness-check.reason: Knowing when a set is behind upstream matters for running many instances over time.

syn-freshness-dismiss.reason: Belongs with the freshness check, a production maintenance feature.

syn-freshness-status.reason: Belongs with the freshness check, a production maintenance feature.

syn-nc-theming-sync.reason: Keeping core theming colours and logo in line avoids two conflicting brands; two competitors rate yes.

syn-nc-theming-edit.reason: Only Nextcloud Theming itself rates yes; admins can edit core theming on its own page.

syn-upgrade-migration.reason: Three competitors rate yes; settings must survive upgrades and the rename from nldesign.

int-capability-api.reason: Exposing the house style to clients and apps is an integration; two competitors rate yes.

int-token-set-api.reason: An API for the catalogue is an integration; two competitors rate yes.

int-stylesheet-manifest.reason: Swapping stylesheets in place is an integration for other apps; no competitor rates yes.

int-metrics.reason: Prometheus metrics are an operations need for running at scale.

int-health.reason: Health checks for monitoring are an operations need for running at scale.

int-tokens-for-other-apps.reason: Two competitors rate yes; other apps must follow the brand through the same CSS variables.

int-no-js-overhead.reason: Three competitors rate yes; theming must not slow down ordinary pages for daily users.

int-rest-api-theme.reason: Decided no: only Microsoft 365 offers it, no demand, outside the core job.

int-cli-set-theme.reason: Two competitors rate yes; command line control matters for scripted deployments.

int-docs-site.reason: Three competitors rate yes; admins need documentation to configure the app themselves.

int-sovereign-bundle.reason: Gap decision defer: no demand, only openDesk rates yes; bundling is MijnBureau or EDIC packaging.

sur-help-links.reason: Decided no: help links are core ThemingDefaults; the request is against Nextcloud server.

sur-support-link.reason: Decided no: footer links are core ThemingDefaults; the request is against Nextcloud server.

sur-localised-name.reason: Decided no: instance name and slogan are core values; the request is against Nextcloud server.

sur-login-wording.reason: Decided no: the login form labels are core; the request is against Nextcloud server.

gov-enforce-appearance.reason: Decided no: enforce_theme is Nextcloud server's own setting.

acc-toast-timeout.reason: Decided no: the toast timeout is a Nextcloud server user setting; per-user settings are a non-goal.

sur-selection-colour.reason: Only a changelog row and one competitor; a visual nicety without real demand.

sur-coverage-report.reason: Decided no: no competitor, one feature request, outside the core job.

sco-suite-wide-appearance.reason: Decided no: the missing half lives in separate office and chat servers thematiq cannot reach.

ast-mobile-logo.reason: A changelog row and one competitor; it only concerns the OpenProject plugin.

gov-environment-marker.reason: A tender row asks for a visible test versus production marker; matters for OTAP at scale.

sur-generated-documents.reason: A tender row asks for house style on generated letters and PDFs; two competitors partly offer it.

gov-token-deprecation.reason: Only Tokens Studio rates yes; matters to set maintainers, not to organisations using the app.

syn-push-to-platform.reason: Decided no: only Tokens Studio offers it, no demand, outside the core job.

aut-dtcg-bulk-convert.reason: Decided no: only Tokens Studio offers it, no demand, outside the core job.

aut-motion-tokens.reason: Only Tokens Studio rates yes and the demand is a changelog row.

typ-theme-base-size.reason: Decided no: only Tokens Studio offers it, no demand, outside the core job.

aut-dtcg-colour-objects.reason: Reading the stable DTCG format keeps imports working as sources move; a migration and import need.

aut-broken-reference-list.reason: A feature request; catching broken references before publishing is hardening for own sets.

cat-living-token-docs.reason: A feature request but no competitor rates yes; nice for maintainers, not needed to theme an instance.

int-brand-kit-in-editor.reason: Decided no: the presentation editor is Collabora or OnlyOffice, out of thematiq's reach.

sco-per-app-login.reason: Decided no: the per-group theming spec requires login pages to use the instance default.

gov-lock-per-space.reason: A roadmap row and one competitor; spaces with their own branding are rare in Nextcloud.

sur-assistant-logo.reason: A roadmap row and one competitor; a small trust signal with little demand.

gov-no-public-cdn.reason: Four competitors rate yes; keeping brand assets off public CDNs is a sovereignty demand in tenders.

ast-branded-reactions.reason: Decided no: meeting reactions are rendered by Nextcloud Talk, not by thematiq.

sur-block-page.reason: Decided no: a network gateway block page is not a Nextcloud page.

sur-per-app-brand.reason: A roadmap row and one competitor; per-app brand names are rare in government deployments.

gov-central-brand-library.reason: One central library used by many departments is a multi-tenant and governance need.

app-branding-package.reason: A roadmap row with no competitor yes; the catalogue already applies a set in one action.

acc-high-contrast-tokens.reason: Decided no: no competitor, one roadmap row, outside the core job.

aut-light-dark-values.reason: Separate light and dark values give fine-grained control for strict brands; one competitor partly offers it.

aut-add-token.reason: A roadmap row with no competitor yes; the bundled vocabulary covers what organisations need.

aut-alpha-hex.reason: One competitor rates yes and the demand is a changelog row.

aut-component-preview.reason: A feature request for component builders, not for organisations theming an instance.

aut-action-colour.reason: Separate action colour is fine-grained control some design systems need; no competitor or demand row.

gov-restricted-set-licence.reason: Keeping licence-restricted sets off until confirmed is legal compliance, needed before wide distribution.

int-shell-tokens.reason: Integration for the OpenProject plugin and other products in a suite deployment.
